t: **Microsoft Entra ID** is Azure's identity service. It answers one question: *who are you?* Every Azure subscription trusts exactly one Entra **tenant**, and a tenant is simply your organization's own directory of users, groups, devices and apps. Think of the tenant as the HR office of a company: it knows the people. The subscription is the building: it holds the equipment. The HR office can serve several buildings, but each building trusts only one HR office.

**Microsoft Entra ID** Azure ki identity service hai. Yeh ek sawal ka jawab deti hai: *aap kaun hain?* Har Azure subscription sirf ek Entra **tenant** par trust karti hai, aur tenant aap ki organization ki apni directory hai jis mein users, groups, devices aur apps hote hain. Tenant ko company ka HR office samjhein: woh logon ko janta hai. Subscription building hai: us mein saman hota hai. Ek HR office kai buildings ko chala sakta hai, lekin har building ek hi HR office par trust karti hai.
Domains and sign-in names
Domains aur sign-in names

A new tenant gets a domain such as `contoso.onmicrosoft.com`. It can never be removed. To let people sign in as `ali@contoso.com`, you add `contoso.com` as a **custom domain** and prove that you own it by creating a **TXT** (or MX) record at your DNS registrar. Only after verification can the domain be used in a **user principal name (UPN)**, which is the sign-in name. The display name is only a label and can be the same for two people.

Naye tenant ko `contoso.onmicrosoft.com` jaisa domain milta hai. Yeh kabhi hataya nahi ja sakta. Log `ali@contoso.com` se sign in karein, is ke liye `contoso.com` ko **custom domain** ke taur par add karte hain aur DNS registrar par **TXT** (ya MX) record bana kar sabit karte hain ke domain aap ka hai. Verify hone ke baad hi domain **user principal name (UPN)** mein chalta hai, jo sign-in naam hai. Display name sirf label hai, do logon ka ek jaisa ho sakta hai.
Kinds of users
Users ki qismein

items: **Cloud-only user**: created in Entra ID and managed there.
**Cloud-only user**: Entra ID mein bana aur wahin manage hota hai.
**Synced (hybrid) user**: created in on-premises Active Directory and copied by Entra Connect. Its source of authority is on-premises, so you change the job title there, not in the cloud.
**Synced (hybrid) user**: on-premises Active Directory mein bana aur Entra Connect se copy hua. Us ka asal source on-premises hai, is liye job title wahan badalte hain, cloud mein nahi.

**Guest (external) user**: invited from another organization (B2B). They sign in with their own account, and you only decide what they may access. By default guests see much less of your directory than members.

**Guest (external) user**: doosri organization se invite kiya gaya (B2B). Woh apne account se sign in karta hai, aap sirf tay karte hain ke kya access ho. Default mein guests ko aap ki directory members se bohat kam nazar aati hai.

t: A deleted user isn't gone at once: for **30 days** it waits under Deleted users and can be restored with its properties and memberships. To stop somebody immediately without deleting them, turn off **Account enabled**. To create many users at once, upload a CSV with **Bulk create**.

Delete kiya user foran khatam nahi hota: **30 din** tak Deleted users mein rehta hai aur apni properties aur memberships ke sath wapas aa sakta hai. Kisi ko delete kiye baghair foran rokne ke liye **Account enabled** band karein. Ek sath bohat se users ke liye **Bulk create** se CSV upload karein.
Entra ID → Users → New user · External Identities → External collaboration settings (who may invite guests, which domains are allowed)
Entra ID → Users → New user · External Identities → External collaboration settings (guests kaun invite kare, kaun se domains allowed)
Groups
Groups

You almost never give access to single people. You put them in a group and give access to the group, so that joining or leaving a team is the only change you make. A **security group** can hold users, devices, service principals and other groups, and it's used for access and licenses. A **Microsoft 365 group** holds only users and comes with a mailbox, Teams and SharePoint.

Aap akele logon ko access taqreeban kabhi nahi dete. Unhein group mein dalte hain aur group ko access dete hain, taa ke team mein aana jana hi wahid tabdeeli ho. **Security group** mein users, devices, service principals aur doosre groups ho sakte hain, aur yeh access aur licenses ke liye hai. **Microsoft 365 group** mein sirf users hote hain, sath mailbox, Teams aur SharePoint milta hai.

Membership can be **Assigned** (by hand) or **Dynamic** (by a rule such as `user.department -eq 'Sales'`). Dynamic membership needs Entra ID **P1**. A dynamic group contains users *or* devices, never both, and nobody can be added by hand because the rule decides.

Membership **Assigned** (haath se) ya **Dynamic** (rule se, jaise `user.department -eq 'Sales'`) hoti hai. Dynamic ke liye Entra ID **P1** chahiye. Dynamic group mein users *ya* devices hote hain, dono nahi, aur haath se koi add nahi hota kyunke faisla rule karta hai.

Sales grows every month. With an assigned group, somebody must remember to add each new seller. With a dynamic group on the department attribute, HR only sets the department and everything else (access, licenses) follows by itself.

Sales har mahine barhta hai. Assigned group mein kisi ko har naya seller yaad se add karna parta hai. Department attribute wale dynamic group mein HR sirf department set karta hai aur baqi sab (access, licenses) khud ho jata hai.
Devices
Devices

**Entra registered** is for personal phones and laptops (BYOD): the person keeps a local sign-in and adds the work account. **Entra joined** is for company devices that live only in the cloud: you sign in to Windows with the work account. **Hybrid joined** is for company devices that are members of an on-premises AD domain and also known to Entra ID, which is what Conditional Access needs for them.

**Entra registered** zaati phones aur laptops (BYOD) ke liye hai: banda local sign-in rakhta hai aur work account add karta hai. **Entra joined** company ke woh devices hain jo sirf cloud mein hain: Windows mein work account se sign in. **Hybrid joined** company ke woh devices hain jo on-premises AD domain ke member bhi hain aur Entra ID ko bhi maloom hain, jo Conditional Access ko un ke liye chahiye.
Administrative units
Administrative units

An Entra role such as Helpdesk Administrator normally applies to the whole tenant. An **administrative unit** is a container of users, groups or devices to which you can limit such a role: the Lahore helpdesk resets passwords only for the Lahore unit.

Helpdesk Administrator jaisa Entra role aam tor par poore tenant par lagta hai. **Administrative unit** users, groups ya devices ka container hai jis tak aisa role mehdood ho sakta hai: Lahore ka helpdesk sirf Lahore unit ke passwords reset kare.
Don't confuse an administrative unit with a resource group. Units hold *people* for Entra roles. Resource groups hold *Azure resources* for Azure roles.
Administrative unit ko resource group se na milayen. Units mein *log* hote hain, Entra roles ke liye. Resource groups mein *Azure resources*, Azure roles ke liye.
A synced user's phone number is wrong. Where do you fix it?
Synced user ka phone number ghalat hai. Kahan theek karenge?
a: In on-premises Active Directory. The cloud copy is overwritten at the next synchronization.
On-premises Active Directory mein. Cloud wali copy agli sync mein overwrite ho jati hai.

t: Why can't you add a colleague to a dynamic group by hand?
Dynamic group mein colleague ko haath se kyun add nahi kar sakte?
a: Because membership comes only from the rule. Change the attribute the rule looks at instead.
Kyunke membership sirf rule se aati hai. Is ki jagah woh attribute badlein jo rule dekhta hai.

t: Your tenant has contoso.com verified. Can two people have the same UPN?
Tenant mein contoso.com verified hai. Kya do logon ka UPN ek ho sakta hai?
a: No. A UPN is unique in the tenant. Display names may repeat.
Nahi. UPN tenant mein unique hota hai. Display name ek jaisa ho sakta hai.

t: A license switches features on for a person. In the exam the question is usually: *which license does this feature need?* Entra ID comes as **Free**, **P1** and **P2**. Learn it as a ladder: P1 adds automation and control, P2 adds protection of powerful accounts.

License kisi shakhs ke liye features on karta hai. Exam mein sawal aam tor par yeh hota hai: *is feature ko kaun sa license chahiye?* Entra ID **Free**, **P1** aur **P2** mein aata hai. Isay seerhi samjhein: P1 automation aur control deta hai, P2 taqatwar accounts ki hifazat.

items: **P1**: dynamic groups, Conditional Access, group-based licensing, password writeback.
**P1**: dynamic groups, Conditional Access, group-based licensing, password writeback.
**P2**: everything in P1 plus **Privileged Identity Management (PIM)**, Identity Protection (risk) and access reviews. If you read *just-in-time*, *approval* or *risk*, think P2.
**P2**: P1 ka sab kuch aur **Privileged Identity Management (PIM)**, Identity Protection (risk) aur access reviews. *Just-in-time*, *approval* ya *risk* likha ho to P2 sochein.

t: Assigning licenses
License dena

You can assign a license to one user, or to a group (**group-based licensing**). With a group, everybody who joins gets the license and everybody who leaves loses it. Two things make it fail. First, the user needs a **Usage location**, because some services aren't allowed in every country. Second, the group's **nested** groups are ignored: only direct members get licenses. If there are 100 licenses and 110 members, 100 are licensed and the other 10 show an error.

License ek user ko ya group ko (**group-based licensing**) diya ja sakta hai. Group mein jo aaye usay mil jata hai, jo jaye us se hat jata hai. Do wajah se fail hota hai. Pehli: user ki **Usage location** honi chahiye, kyunke kuch services har mulk mein allowed nahi. Doosri: group ke **nested** groups nahi gine jate, sirf seedhe members. 100 license aur 110 members hon to 100 ko mil jata hai, baqi 10 par error aata hai.
Inside a license you can switch off single service plans, for example give Microsoft 365 E3 to a group without Exchange Online.
License ke andar akele service plans band kiye ja sakte hain, maslan group ko Microsoft 365 E3 dein lekin Exchange Online ke baghair.
Self-service password reset (SSPR)
Self-service password reset (SSPR)
SSPR lets people reset a forgotten password themselves at `aka.ms/sspr`, after proving who they are. It saves the helpdesk its most common call. You set three things:
SSPR se log `aka.ms/sspr` par apni pehchan sabit kar ke khud bhoola password reset karte hain. Is se helpdesk ki sab se aam call bachti hai. Teen cheezein set hoti hain:

items: **Who**: None, Selected (exactly **one** group, which may contain nested groups) or All.
**Kaun**: None, Selected (bilkul **ek** group, jis mein nested groups ho sakte hain) ya All.
**How**: which methods are allowed (authenticator app, phone, email, security questions…) and whether 1 or 2 are required.
**Kaise**: kaun se tareeqe allowed (authenticator app, phone, email, security questions…) aur 1 ya 2 lazmi.
**Registration**: whether people must register their methods at the next sign-in, and how often they confirm them.
**Registration**: kya agle sign-in par tareeqe register karna lazmi hai, aur kitne din baad dobara confirm.

t: Administrators have their own, stronger policy that you can't weaken: always **two** methods and never security questions.
Administrators ki apni sakht policy hai jo kamzor nahi ho sakti: hamesha **do** tareeqe aur security questions kabhi nahi.
Password writeback
Password writeback

For synced users the password lives on-premises. A reset in the cloud alone would leave the old password valid on the domain. **Writeback** sends the new password back to on-premises AD. It needs P1 and must be switched on in **two places**: in Entra Connect, and in Password reset → On-premises integration. If people can reset but the new password doesn't work on the office PC, one of the two is off.

Synced users ka password on-premises hota hai. Sirf cloud mein reset se domain par purana password chalta rehta. **Writeback** naya password on-premises AD ko bhejta hai. Is ke liye P1 chahiye aur **do jagah** on karna hota hai: Entra Connect mein, aur Password reset → On-premises integration mein. Log reset kar lein lekin office PC par naya password na chale to in mein se ek band hai.
Entra ID → Licenses · Entra ID → Password reset → Properties / Authentication methods / Registration / On-premises integration
Entra ID → Licenses · Entra ID → Password reset → Properties / Authentication methods / Registration / On-premises integration

A company enables SSPR for a pilot. They can choose only one group in Selected, so they create 'SSPR-Pilot' and put the two pilot departments in it as nested groups. Works: SSPR accepts nesting here, unlike licensing.

Company SSPR ka pilot chalati hai. Selected mein ek hi group chun sakte hain, is liye 'SSPR-Pilot' bana kar dono pilot departments us mein nested dalte hain. Chalta hai: SSPR yahan nesting leta hai, licensing nahi leti.
SSPR is about *forgotten passwords*. Multi-factor authentication is about *signing in*. They share registration but are different features.
SSPR *bhoole password* ke liye hai. Multi-factor authentication *sign in* ke liye. Registration shared hai lekin feature alag hain.
A license can't be assigned to a new user. What do you check first?
Naye user ko license nahi lag raha. Sab se pehle kya dekhenge?
a: The user's Usage location.
User ki Usage location.

t: A question says administrators must activate the Owner role for two hours with approval. Which license?
Sawal kehta hai admins Owner role do ghante ke liye approval se activate karein. Kaun sa license?
a: Entra ID P2, because that is Privileged Identity Management.
Entra ID P2, kyunke yeh Privileged Identity Management hai.

t: How many groups can you select for SSPR?
SSPR ke liye kitne groups chun sakte hain?
a: One, but it may contain nested groups.
Ek, lekin us mein nested groups ho sakte hain.

t: **Azure RBAC** answers *what may you do with Azure resources?* A **role assignment** joins three things: **who** (a user, group, service principal or managed identity), **what** (a role definition, which is a list of allowed actions) and **where** (the scope). Leave one out and there's no access. Compare it with a hotel: the guest is who, the kind of key card is what, and the floor is where.

**Azure RBAC** is sawal ka jawab hai: *Azure resources ke sath aap kya kar sakte hain?* **Role assignment** teen cheezein jorta hai: **kaun** (user, group, service principal ya managed identity), **kya** (role definition, yani allowed actions ki list) aur **kahan** (scope). Ek bhi na ho to access nahi. Hotel se samjhein: mehmaan kaun hai, key card ki qism kya hai, aur manzil kahan hai.
Scope and inheritance
Scope aur inheritance

Scopes form a ladder: **management group → subscription → resource group → resource**. An assignment works at its scope and at everything below it, never above and never sideways. A Reader on the subscription reads every resource group in it. A Contributor on RG1 has nothing in RG2. Best practice: assign to **groups**, at the **smallest** scope that does the job.

Scopes seerhi hain: **management group → subscription → resource group → resource**. Assignment apne scope aur us se neeche sab par chalta hai, na upar na bagal mein. Subscription ka Reader us ke har resource group ko parhta hai. RG1 ke Contributor ka RG2 mein kuch nahi. Achha tareeqa: **groups** ko dein, **sab se chhote** kaafi scope par.
The four basic roles
Chaar bunyadi roles

items: **Owner**: everything, including giving access to others.
**Owner**: sab kuch, doosron ko access dena bhi.
**Contributor**: manage all resources, but *not* give access.
**Contributor**: tamam resources manage, lekin access dena *nahi*.
**Reader**: look, don't touch.
**Reader**: dekho, chhuo mat.
**User Access Administrator**: give access, but not manage resources.
**User Access Administrator**: access dena, resources manage nahi.

t: Control plane and data plane
Control plane aur data plane

This is the idea people get wrong most often. The **control plane** manages the resource itself (create the storage account, change its settings). The **data plane** works with what's inside (read a blob, read a secret). Owner and Contributor are control-plane roles: they contain no blob *data* actions. To read blobs with your Entra sign-in you need a data role such as **Storage Blob Data Reader**. A Contributor can often still see blobs, but only because they can fetch the account *key*. Turn off shared key access and that back door closes.

Isi baat mein sab se zyada ghalti hoti hai. **Control plane** resource ko manage karta hai (storage account banana, settings badalna). **Data plane** us ke andar ki cheez (blob parhna, secret parhna). Owner aur Contributor control-plane roles hain: un mein blob *data* actions nahi. Entra sign-in se blobs parhne ke liye **Storage Blob Data Reader** jaisa data role chahiye. Contributor aksar blobs phir bhi dekh leta hai, lekin sirf is liye ke woh account ki *key* le sakta hai. Shared key access band karein to yeh raasta bhi band.
How Azure decides
Azure faisla kaise karta hai

First Azure looks for a **deny assignment**. If one applies, access is blocked, even for an Owner. You don't create these by hand in IAM: they come from things like deployment stacks. Then Azure adds up **all** role assignments of the user and their groups (nested groups count). Roles are **additive**: the result is the sum, there's no 'most restrictive role wins'.

Pehle Azure **deny assignment** dekhta hai. Lagta ho to access band, Owner ke liye bhi. Yeh IAM mein haath se nahi bante: deployment stacks jaisi cheezon se aate hain. Phir Azure user aur us ke groups ke **tamam** role assignments jama karta hai (nested groups bhi). Roles **additive** hain: nateeja majmua hai, 'sab se sakht role jeetta hai' jaisi baat nahi.
Custom roles
Custom roles

When no built-in role fits, write your own in JSON: `Actions` (allowed control-plane operations), `NotActions` (taken out of Actions), `DataActions`, `NotDataActions` and `AssignableScopes`. `NotActions` is **not a deny**: it only subtracts from this one role, so another role can still grant the action. Custom roles can't be assigned at the root scope `/`.

Koi built-in role na bethe to JSON mein apna likhein: `Actions` (allowed control-plane operations), `NotActions` (Actions mein se nikale), `DataActions`, `NotDataActions` aur `AssignableScopes`. `NotActions` **deny nahi**: sirf isi role se ghatata hai, doosra role woh action de sakta hai. Custom roles root scope `/` par nahi lagte.

Helpdesk must see and restart VMs in RG1. Virtual Machine Contributor works, but also lets them delete VMs. A custom role with `Microsoft.Compute/virtualMachines/read` and `.../restart/action` on RG1 is true least privilege.

Helpdesk ko RG1 ki VMs dekhni aur restart karni hain. Virtual Machine Contributor chal jayega, lekin VM delete bhi karne dega. RG1 par `Microsoft.Compute/virtualMachines/read` aur `.../restart/action` wala custom role asli least privilege hai.
Entra roles are a different list
Entra roles alag list hain

**Entra roles** (Global Administrator, User Administrator…) manage the *directory*. **Azure roles** (Owner, Contributor…) manage *resources*. A Global Administrator has no Azure access by default, but can turn on *Access management for Azure resources* (**elevate access**). That gives User Access Administrator at the root scope, so they can assign roles, including to themselves, in every subscription. Switch it off when done.

**Entra roles** (Global Administrator, User Administrator…) *directory* manage karte hain. **Azure roles** (Owner, Contributor…) *resources*. Global Administrator ke paas default mein Azure access nahi, lekin woh *Access management for Azure resources* (**elevate access**) on kar sakta hai. Is se root scope par User Access Administrator milta hai, aur woh har subscription mein roles de sakta hai, khud ko bhi. Kaam ke baad band karein.
Managed identity, PIM and conditions
Managed identity, PIM aur conditions

A **managed identity** is an identity for an Azure resource such as a VM. Azure handles its secret, so your app signs in to Key Vault or Storage with no password in its code. *System-assigned* lives and dies with the resource; *user-assigned* is a separate resource that several can share. With **PIM**, a user gets an *eligible* role and activates it only when needed (P2; at management group, subscription or resource group scope; users only). With **conditions (ABAC)** you narrow a blob or queue data role, for example to blobs with a certain tag. A condition never denies: an unconditional assignment next to it still wins.

**Managed identity** VM jaise Azure resource ki identity hai. Us ka secret Azure sambhalta hai, is liye app code mein password ke baghair Key Vault ya Storage mein sign in karti hai. *System-assigned* resource ke sath marti hai; *user-assigned* alag resource hai jo kai use kar sakte hain. **PIM** mein user ko *eligible* role milta hai jo zaroorat par activate hota hai (P2; management group, subscription ya resource group scope par; sirf users). **Conditions (ABAC)** se blob ya queue data role mehdood hota hai, maslan sirf kisi tag wale blobs. Condition deny nahi karti: sath wala baghair condition assignment phir bhi sab de deta hai.
Any resource → Access control (IAM) → Check access / Add role assignment / Role assignments
Koi bhi resource → Access control (IAM) → Check access / Add role assignment / Role assignments
Moving a subscription to another tenant deletes **all** its role assignments. 'Identity not found' in IAM means the user or app was deleted.
Subscription doosre tenant mein le jane se us ke **tamam** role assignments khatam ho jate hain. IAM mein 'Identity not found' ka matlab user ya app delete ho chuka.
You're Reader on Sub1 and Contributor on RG1. Can you create a VM in RG2?
Aap Sub1 par Reader aur RG1 par Contributor hain. Kya RG2 mein VM bana sakte hain?
a: No. In RG2 you have only the inherited Reader.
Nahi. RG2 mein sirf inherit hua Reader hai.

t: Which built-in roles can give access to others?
Kaun se built-in roles doosron ko access de sakte hain?
a: Owner and User Access Administrator (and the newer Role Based Access Control Administrator). Contributor can't.
Owner aur User Access Administrator (aur naya Role Based Access Control Administrator). Contributor nahi.

t: An app on a VM needs a secret from Key Vault. How do you avoid storing a password?
VM ki app ko Key Vault se secret chahiye. Password rakhne se kaise bachenge?
a: Give the VM a managed identity and grant that identity access to the vault.
VM ko managed identity dein aur us identity ko vault ka access.

t: RBAC controls *people*. **Azure Policy** controls *resources*: what may be created and how it must look. A policy says things like 'only in West Europe', 'every resource needs a tag', 'diagnostic settings must be on'. It's checked for everybody, so even an Owner can't create something a Deny policy forbids.

RBAC *logon* ko control karta hai. **Azure Policy** *resources* ko: kya ban sakta hai aur kaisa ho. Policy kehti hai 'sirf West Europe', 'har resource par tag', 'diagnostic settings on hon'. Yeh sab par lagti hai, is liye Deny policy ke khilaf Owner bhi kuch nahi bana sakta.
The pieces
Hisse

items: **Definition**: one rule (if … then effect). There are hundreds of built-in ones.
**Definition**: ek rule (if … then effect). Sainkron built-in maujood hain.
**Initiative**: a group of definitions assigned as one, for example a whole security standard.
**Initiative**: definitions ka group jo ek sath assign ho, maslan poora security standard.
**Assignment**: the definition or initiative put on a scope (management group, subscription or resource group), with parameters.
**Assignment**: definition ya initiative ko scope (management group, subscription ya resource group) par lagana, parameters ke sath.
**Exclusion**: a child scope that isn't evaluated at all. **Exemption**: a resource that is evaluated but marked Exempt, with a reason and often an end date.
**Exclusion**: child scope jo evaluate hi nahi hota. **Exemption**: resource jo evaluate hota hai lekin Exempt mark hota hai, wajah aur aksar aakhri tareekh ke sath.

t: Effects, in plain words
Effects, aasan lafzon mein

items: **Deny**: the request is refused.
**Deny**: request mana.
**Audit**: allowed, but reported as non-compliant.
**Audit**: allowed, lekin non-compliant report.
**Modify / Append**: the request is changed on its way in, for example a tag is added. Modify can also repair existing resources.
**Modify / Append**: request andar aate hue badalti hai, maslan tag lag jata hai. Modify mojooda resources bhi theek kar sakta hai.
**DeployIfNotExists**: if something related is missing (an agent, a diagnostic setting), it's deployed.
**DeployIfNotExists**: related cheez (agent, diagnostic setting) na ho to deploy ho jati hai.
**AuditIfNotExists**: the same check, but only reported.
**AuditIfNotExists**: wahi check, lekin sirf report.
**denyAction**: blocks an action on existing resources. Today that action is delete.
**denyAction**: mojooda resources par action rokta hai. Abhi woh action delete hai.
**Disabled**: the rule does nothing.
**Disabled**: rule kuch nahi karta.

t: Order matters. For a create or update, Modify and Append run **before** Deny. So a Modify policy that adds a tag satisfies a Deny policy that demands it.
Tarteeb ahem hai. Create ya update par Modify aur Append **Deny se pehle** chalte hain. Is liye tag lagane wali Modify policy us tag ko mangne wali Deny policy ko mutmain kar deti hai.
Existing resources and remediation
Mojooda resources aur remediation

Assigning a policy never deletes or stops anything. Existing resources that break the rule are only marked **non-compliant**. To repair them with Modify or DeployIfNotExists you start a **remediation task**. It runs under the assignment's **managed identity**, which needs the right role at the scope. 'Remediation fails with an authorization error' almost always means that identity has no role.

Policy assign karne se kuch delete ya band nahi hota. Rule tornay wale mojooda resources sirf **non-compliant** mark hote hain. Modify ya DeployIfNotExists se unhein theek karne ke liye **remediation task** chalate hain. Woh assignment ki **managed identity** se chalta hai, jisay scope par sahi role chahiye. 'Remediation authorization error se fail' ka matlab taqreeban hamesha yeh hai ke identity ke paas role nahi.

When is it checked? When a resource is created or updated, when a policy is newly assigned, and in a full scan about every **24 hours**. You can start a scan with `az policy state trigger-scan`. A new assignment can need some minutes before it blocks anything.

Kab check hota hai? Resource create ya update hone par, policy nayi assign hone par, aur taqreeban har **24 ghante** poore scan mein. `az policy state trigger-scan` se scan khud chala sakte hain. Naye assignment ko rokna shuru karne mein chand minute lag sakte hain.

You want a Deny policy but fear breaking things. Assign it with **enforcement mode Disabled (DoNotEnforce)**: compliance is reported, nothing is blocked. When the report looks right, enable enforcement.

Aap Deny policy lagana chahte hain lekin dar hai kuch toot jaye. **Enforcement mode Disabled (DoNotEnforce)** ke sath assign karein: compliance report hoti hai, kuch block nahi hota. Report theek lage to enforcement on karein.
Policy → Definitions / Assignments / Compliance / Remediation
Policy → Definitions / Assignments / Compliance / Remediation
Two policies never cancel each other. If one allows only East US and another denies East US, nothing can be deployed: the result is the cumulative most restrictive.
Do policies ek doosri ko khatam nahi karti. Ek sirf East US allow kare aur doosri East US deny, to kuch deploy nahi hoga: nateeja sab ka mila kar sab se sakht hota hai.
A Deny policy for public IPs is assigned. What happens to the 10 existing public IPs?
Public IP ki Deny policy assign hui. Pehle se mojood 10 public IPs ka kya hoga?
a: Nothing, except that they're reported as non-compliant.
Kuch nahi, sirf non-compliant report honge.

t: Which effects need a managed identity?
Kaun se effects ko managed identity chahiye?
a: DeployIfNotExists and Modify, because they change resources.
DeployIfNotExists aur Modify, kyunke yeh resources badalte hain.

t: Exclusion or exemption: the security team wants to see the resource in the report with a reason.
Exclusion ya exemption: security team resource ko wajah ke sath report mein dekhna chahti hai.
a: Exemption. An excluded scope isn't evaluated at all.
Exemption. Excluded scope evaluate hi nahi hota.

t: Resource groups: the life-cycle box
Resource groups: zindagi ka dabba

A **resource group** is a box for resources that live and die together. Deleting the box deletes everything in it. Every resource is in exactly one group. The group has a region only because its *metadata* must be stored somewhere: the resources inside can be in any region. Put a web app, its database and its storage in one group if you deploy and delete them together.

**Resource group** un resources ka dabba hai jo sath jeete sath marte hain. Dabba delete karein to andar sab delete. Har resource theek ek group mein hota hai. Group ka region sirf is liye hai ke us ka *metadata* kahin rakhna hota hai: andar ke resources kisi bhi region mein ho sakte hain. Web app, database aur storage sath deploy aur delete hote hon to ek group mein rakhein.
Moving resources
Resources move karna

Most resources can be moved to another group or subscription. Remember four rules: the **region doesn't change**; the **resource ID changes**, so scripts and alerts that use it must be updated; both groups are **locked for changes** during the move (the resources keep running); and for another subscription, both must be in the **same tenant** and the resource provider must be registered in the target. *Validate move* checks all this without moving. Dependent resources (a VM's disks and NIC) go along.

Aksar resources doosre group ya subscription mein move ho sakte hain. Chaar usool: **region nahi badalta**; **resource ID badalti hai**, is liye us par chalne wale scripts aur alerts badalne hote hain; move ke dauran dono groups **tabdeeli ke liye lock** hote hain (resources chalte rehte hain); aur doosri subscription ke liye dono **same tenant** mein hon aur target mein resource provider registered ho. *Validate move* baghair move kiye yeh sab dekhta hai. Dependent resources (VM ki disks aur NIC) sath jate hain.
Locks
Locks

A **lock** protects against accidents, not against bad intentions: it applies to everybody, Owners too, until someone with permission removes it. **CanNotDelete** allows reading and changing but not deleting. **ReadOnly** allows only reading. Locks are inherited by everything below, and the most restrictive one wins. You can't put one on a management group.

**Lock** ghalti se bachata hai, bad-niyyati se nahi: yeh sab par lagta hai, Owner par bhi, jab tak permission wala usay hata na de. **CanNotDelete** parhna aur badalna deta hai, delete nahi. **ReadOnly** sirf parhna. Locks neeche sab ko inherit hote hain, aur sab se sakht jeetta hai. Management group par nahi lagta.

ReadOnly surprises people, because Azure treats every **POST** as a write. Starting or restarting a VM is a POST, and so is *listing storage account keys*. With ReadOnly on a storage account, tools that need the key stop working, while somebody with a blob data role can still upload, because locks cover only the control plane.

ReadOnly hairan karta hai, kyunke Azure har **POST** ko write samajhta hai. VM start ya restart POST hai, aur *storage account keys list karna* bhi. Storage account par ReadOnly ho to key mangne wale tools band ho jate hain, jab ke blob data role wala phir bhi upload kar sakta hai, kyunke locks sirf control plane par hain.
To create or delete locks you need `Microsoft.Authorization/locks/*`, which **Owner** and **User Access Administrator** have. Contributor doesn't.
Locks banane ya hatane ke liye `Microsoft.Authorization/locks/*` chahiye, jo **Owner** aur **User Access Administrator** ke paas hai. Contributor ke paas nahi.
Tags
Tags

A **tag** is a label such as `costcenter=100`. Up to 50 per resource, group or subscription. Names ignore upper and lower case, values don't. Tags have two big uses: **cost reports** (group by tag in Cost analysis) and automation (shut down everything with `env=dev`). They are **not inherited**. If resources must carry their group's tag, use the built-in policy *Inherit a tag from the resource group*. For cost reports alone, Cost Management has its own *tag inheritance* setting, which applies tags to usage records without touching the resources.

**Tag** `costcenter=100` jaisa label hai. Har resource, group ya subscription par 50 tak. Naam mein bare chhote harf ka farq nahi, value mein hai. Do bare istemal: **cost reports** (Cost analysis mein tag se group) aur automation (`env=dev` wala sab band). Yeh **inherit nahi hote**. Resources par group ka tag lazmi ho to built-in policy *Inherit a tag from the resource group*. Sirf cost reports ke liye Cost Management ki apni *tag inheritance* setting hai, jo resources ko chhere baghair usage records par tag lagati hai.
You delete RG1 and get an error, although you're Owner and RG1 has no lock. One VM inside has a CanNotDelete lock. Deleting the group would delete the VM, so the whole operation is refused.

Aap RG1 delete karte hain aur error aata hai, halanke aap Owner hain aur RG1 par lock nahi. Andar ek VM par CanNotDelete lock hai. Group delete karne se VM bhi jati, is liye poora kaam mana ho jata hai.
Resource or group → Locks · Tags · Move · Resource group → Settings
Resource ya group → Locks · Tags · Move · Resource group → Settings
**Tags don't inherit, locks do.** If you remember one line of this page, take this one. And `az tag create` replaces all tags, while `az tag update --operation Merge` keeps the others.
**Tags inherit nahi hote, locks hote hain.** Is page se ek line yaad rakhni ho to yeh. Aur `az tag create` tamam tags badal deta hai, jab ke `az tag update --operation Merge` baqi rakhta hai.
Can a resource group in West Europe contain a VM in East US?
Kya West Europe ka resource group East US ki VM rakh sakta hai?
a: Yes. The group's region stores only metadata.
Haan. Group ka region sirf metadata ke liye hai.

t: A ReadOnly lock is on a VM. The Owner tries to start it.
VM par ReadOnly lock hai. Owner usay start karta hai.
a: It fails: start is a POST action.
Fail: start POST action hai.

t: You moved a VM to another group and an alert stopped. Why?
VM doosre group mein move ki aur alert band ho gaya. Kyun?
a: The resource ID changed, and the alert still points to the old one.
Resource ID badal gayi, aur alert purani par hai.

t: Management groups
Management groups

A **subscription** is a billing and limits boundary: one invoice, its own quotas. Companies use several to separate production from test, or departments. **Management groups** sit above subscriptions so that you set access and policy once. The tree has up to **six levels** below the root, and every management group and subscription has exactly **one parent**. The **tenant root group** is at the top, can't be moved or deleted, and new subscriptions land there unless you choose another default.

**Subscription** billing aur limits ki hadd hai: ek invoice, apne quotas. Companies production aur test, ya departments alag karne ke liye kai rakhti hain. **Management groups** subscriptions ke upar hote hain taa ke access aur policy ek dafa set ho. Root ke neeche **che levels** tak, aur har management group aur subscription ka theek **ek parent**. **Tenant root group** sab se upar hai, move ya delete nahi hota, aur nayi subscriptions wahin aati hain jab tak doosra default na chunein.

Everything you assign at a management group is **inherited**, not copied. Move a subscription to another management group and the old policies and roles stop applying at once, and the new parent's start.
Management group par jo lagayen woh **inherit** hota hai, copy nahi. Subscription doosre management group mein le jayen to purani policies aur roles foran lagna band, naye parent ke shuru.

60 subscriptions need the same 'allowed locations' rule, and next month there will be 65. Assign it once at the management group and make that group the default for new subscriptions. This is the standard answer to 'least administrative effort'.

60 subscriptions ko ek hi 'allowed locations' rule chahiye, aur agle mahine 65 hongi. Management group par ek dafa assign karein aur usay nayi subscriptions ka default banayen. 'Least administrative effort' ka aam jawab yehi hai.
Subscriptions and tenants
Subscriptions aur tenants

A subscription trusts one tenant; a tenant can have many subscriptions. Transferring a subscription to another tenant removes all its role assignments, because the people in them don't exist in the new directory. Quotas (vCPUs per region and so on) belong to a subscription and region: `QuotaExceeded` means you ask for more under **Usage + quotas**. `MissingSubscriptionRegistration` means the **resource provider** isn't registered.

Subscription ek tenant par trust karti hai; tenant ki kai subscriptions ho sakti hain. Subscription doosre tenant ko dene se tamam role assignments hat jate hain, kyunke un ke log nayi directory mein nahi. Quotas (har region ke vCPUs waghera) subscription aur region ke hote hain: `QuotaExceeded` ka matlab **Usage + quotas** mein zyada mangein. `MissingSubscriptionRegistration` ka matlab **resource provider** registered nahi.
Controlling cost
Kharcha control karna

items: **Pricing calculator**: an estimate before you build.
**Pricing calculator**: banane se pehle andaza.
**Cost analysis**: what you really spend, grouped by service, resource group or tag, with a forecast.
**Cost analysis**: asal kharcha, service, resource group ya tag se group, forecast ke sath.
**Budget**: a threshold with alerts, on actual or forecasted cost. It can notify people and trigger an action group.
**Budget**: alerts wali hadd, asal ya forecast kharche par. Logon ko khabar deta aur action group chalata hai.
**Advisor**: personal recommendations in five areas: Cost, Security, Reliability, Operational excellence and Performance. Under Cost it finds idle and oversized VMs.
**Advisor**: paanch shobon mein mashwara: Cost, Security, Reliability, Operational excellence aur Performance. Cost mein khaali aur zyada bari VMs dhoondta hai.

t: **A budget never stops anything by itself.** When spending passes 100% the resources keep running. To stop VMs automatically, connect the budget alert to an action group that runs an Automation runbook or a Function.

**Budget khud kuch band nahi karta.** Kharcha 100% se guzar jaye to bhi resources chalte rehte hain. VMs khud band karne ke liye budget alert ko aise action group se jorein jo Automation runbook ya Function chalaye.
Paying less
Kam paisa dena

**Reservations** give a discount for committing to one or three years of a VM size: for machines that run all the time. A **savings plan** commits to an amount per hour and is more flexible. **Spot** VMs use spare capacity very cheaply but can be evicted: for work that may be interrupted. **Azure Hybrid Benefit** reuses your existing Windows Server or SQL licenses. And for test machines: deallocate them at night.

**Reservations** ek ya teen saal ke waade par VM size ki chhoot dete hain: har waqt chalne wali machines ke liye. **Savings plan** per hour raqam ka waada hai, zyada flexible. **Spot** VMs khaali capacity bohat sasti use karti hain lekin nikali ja sakti hain: rukne wale kaam ke liye. **Azure Hybrid Benefit** aap ke mojooda Windows Server ya SQL licenses use karta hai. Aur test machines: raat ko deallocate karein.
Management groups · Subscriptions → Usage + quotas / Resource providers · Cost Management → Cost analysis / Budgets · Advisor
Management groups · Subscriptions → Usage + quotas / Resource providers · Cost Management → Cost analysis / Budgets · Advisor
'Alert when the *forecast* passes the budget' and 'alert when *actual* cost passes it' are different settings. Read the exhibit carefully.
'*Forecast* budget se guzre to alert' aur '*asal* kharcha guzre to alert' alag settings hain. Exhibit ghaur se parhein.
Can a subscription belong to two management groups?
Kya subscription do management groups mein ho sakti hai?
a: No, exactly one parent.
Nahi, theek ek parent.

t: A VM runs 24/7 for three years. Cheapest option?
VM teen saal 24/7 chalegi. Sab se sasta?
a: A three-year reservation.
Teen saal ki reservation.

t: A deployment fails with QuotaExceeded. What now?
Deployment QuotaExceeded se fail. Ab?
a: Request a quota increase for that region under Usage + quotas, or use another region or size.
Usage + quotas mein us region ka quota barhwayen, ya doosra region ya size use karein.
